Class BotClient

java.lang.Object
de.lmu.dbs.ifi.sep25.network.Client
de.lmu.dbs.ifi.sep25.ui.bot.BotClient
public class BotClient extends Client
A headless client that participates in a RoboRally game as a bot, using a provided BotStrategy.

This client automatically responds to all game decisions using the chosen strategy and never displays a UI. It is intended for automated gameplay, testing, and AI matches.

  • Method Details

    • delayedDecision

      protected void delayedDecision(int delaySeconds, Runnable decisionLogic)
      Schedules the given decision logic to run after the specified delay in seconds, simulating human-like reaction time for all bot actions.

      This method ensures the provided Runnable is executed on a background thread after the specified number of seconds. Typical usage is to wrap all server-response actions (such as card selection, starting position selection, reboot direction, etc.) for realism.

      Parameters:
      delaySeconds - the delay before executing the logic, in seconds
      decisionLogic - the logic to execute after the delay (e.g., sending a move to the server)

    • delayedDecision

      protected void delayedDecision(Runnable decisionLogic)
      Schedules the given decision logic to run after the default decision delay, simulating human-like reaction time for all bot actions.

      This is a convenience overload that uses DEFAULT_DECISION_DELAY_SECONDS as the delay value. Typical usage is to wrap all server-response actions (such as card selection, starting position selection, reboot direction, etc.) for realism.

      Parameters:
      decisionLogic - the logic to execute after the delay (e.g., sending a move to the server)
      See Also:

    • closeAll

      public void closeAll()
      Releases resources associated with the client connection. Also closes scheduler.

      This method ensures the proper closure of the input stream `reader`, output stream `writer`, and the socket connection. It first checks if each resource is non-null (or in the case of the socket, not already closed), and closes them in sequence. If an error occurs during this process, an error message is logged to the standard error stream.

      This method is typically called to clean up resources when the client disconnects or an issue occurs, ensuring no resource leaks.

      Overrides:
